contexts.text: He carried a vessel (of poison) in his hand.
The vessels of the house of God () = holy things (profaned).

Scientifics are general vessels... (Thus) the vessels are one thing, and the essentials in the vessels are another; the vessels are natural things, and the essentials in the vessels are spiritual and celestial things. So also the historicals of the Word, and also all the several words in it, are general, natural, nay, material vessels, in which are spiritual and celestial things.
Therefore scientifics are vessels of spiritual things; and affections from the good pleasures of the body are vessels of celestial things.

By means of Knowledges, the way is opened for the internal man to the external, in which are the recipient vessels, which are as many as are the Knowledges of good and truth. Celestial things inflow into these Knowledges as into their vessels.

For in the external man there are recipient vessels, which are called the things of the memory. These vessels are formed by means of Knowledges... But with the Lord the interiors were celestial, which adapted the vessels for the reception of Knowledges, and so that the Knowledges might afterwards become vessels for the reception of the Divine.
Scientifics, that is, natural Truths, are vessels for spiritual Truths.

Scientifics and Knowledges... are not truths, but are only the recipient vessels; just as whatever is in the memory... is by no means truth... but truth is therein, as in vessels. These vessels were to be formed, or rather opened, by the Lord, by means of instruction in Knowledges from the Word...
The knowledge of Knowledges is merely something instrumental... that they may serve celestial and spiritual things as vessels. Explained.
The Scientific in general then becomes the ultimate vessel; or, what is the same, scientifics in special and particular become the ultimate vessels, which correspond to rational things...

As the way is opened, or, what is the same, as the vessels are opened, there inflow, in order, from celestial and spiritual things, rational things; into these, celestial spiritual things; and into these, celestial things. These latter are continually... preparing for themselves, and forming, the vessels which are being opened. Explained.
The truth learned from childhood, regarded in itself, is merely a vessel so adapted that what is celestial can be insinuated into it. Explained.
For revelation, or the Word, is a general vessel recipient of spiritual and celestial things.
Thus the most tender vessels (of little boys and girls) are almost heavenly...

Thus do (spiritual things) form their vessels or recipients in man. Most of these appear like truths, but are not; such as the things of the literal sense... and some are even falsities, which, however, can serve as vessels and recipients. But with the Lord there are none but truths which are essentially so, and therefore no parallelism and correspondence are possible; but still they can be so adapted as to serve the celestial things of love and charity as vessels.
Yet (these apparent truths of the literal sense) can serve as general vessels to contain spiritual and celestial things. Explained.

Man's life itself is from the internal man, and it can have only a very obscure communication with the external man, until the recipient vessels of the memory have been formed, which is done by means of cognitions and scientifics. Explained.
But this life becomes gradually more distinct as the vessels of the memory are formed by means of Knowledges, and the vessels of the interior memory by means of rational things. Explained.
(Truths) are the genuine vessels in the organic forms of both memories, to which can be adapted the celestial things of love and the spiritual things of faith. (Explained.)
For the things in the memory and the affection of man are recipient vessels, in which the ideas are varied and received representatively according to their variations of form and changes of state.
For all truths are vessels recipient of good... AC 2261:end. AC 5212.

The more genuine and pure a truth is, the better can the good which is from the Lord be fitted to it as its recipient vessel... Goods cannot possibly be insinuated into falsities, nor evils into truths, as their recipient vessels. Explained.
His vessels in the house () = the truths which are of good. To go down to take them away = to turn away from good to truth.
Vessels of adorning of gold and silver () = Knowledges of good and truth from the Word.
To be emptied from vessel to vessel () = (not to be reformed)... The good itself is called the vessel in which there is no pleasure ().
Vessels of brass () = the natural goods which receive the life from the Lord.

A pitcher is a vessel which contains water, as a scientific is a vessel which contains truth; for every scientific is a vessel for truth; and every truth is a vessel for good. A scientific without truth is an empty vessel; and so is truth without good; whereas a scientific in which there is truth, or a truth in which there is good, is a full vessel. AC 3079.
That vessels in general = things which are for receptacles... Illustrated.

The vessels of the Temple and of the altar were holy on account of this their signification... and it was for this reason that when Belshazzar... drank wine out of them... and praised the gods... the writing appeared on the wall. The vessels of gold and silver here = the Knowledges of good and truth, which were profaned. Explained.
That vessels = the externals of spiritual things. Illustrated.

An offering in a clean vessel () is a representative of the external man in relation to the internal man... for a clean vessel = a concordant external; thus the things in the external, which are scientifics, Knowledges, and doctrinals.
Empty vessels () = Knowledges in which there is no truth; and also truths in which there is no good.
That the wise virgins took oil in their vessels () = that there was good in the truths, thus charity in the faith.
Submission of the recipient [vessels]. Signified, Explained.

The servant brought forth vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments () = truth and good and their adornments... Vessels are mentioned because they are predicated of the affection of truth... for, regarded in itself, truth is nothing but a vessel or recipient of good. Vessels of silver = in special, scientifics, for these are recipients of truth; vessels of gold = in special, truths, because these are recipients of good.

Man is a mere organ, or vessel, which receive the life from the Divine... This life is from His Divine love... and it flows in and applies itself to the vessels which are in the Rational, and to those which are in the Natural, of man. These vessels, from evil... are in a contrary situation relatively to that life; yet in so far as the life which inflows is able to dispose the vessels to receive it, it does so dispose them. These vessels in the rational man, and in the natural man, are what are called truths, but in themselves they are merely perceptions of the variations of form of these vessels, and of the changes of state according to which, in various ways, the variations come forth, which take place in the most subtle substances, in inexpressible ways. It is the good itself, in which there is life from the Lord... which inflows and disposes them.

As, therefore, these vessels, which are to be varied according to forms, are in a contrary situation... it is evident that they must be reduced to a situation which accords with the life. This is impossible so long as the man is in the state in which he was born... because they are obstinately resistent... Therefore they must be softened, (which) is effected through temptations... And when the vessels are somewhat tempered and subdued... they begin to become yielding and compliant to the life of the Lord's love which is continually flowing in.
(Thus) doctrinal things are merely appearances of truth Divine, that is, they are merely celestial and spiritual vessels, in which is what is Divine...
For the good from the Lord... can inflow only into truths; for truths are vessels for good.
For Knowledges, being of the natural man, are vessels recipient of rational things.

The Knowledges learned in early childhood are as it were most general vessels, which ought to be filled with goods, and the man is illustrated in proportion as they are so filled. If the vessels are such, that genuine goods can be in them, the man is illustrated by the Divine which is within them... But if they are such that genuine goods cannot be in them, he is not illuminated...
Knowledges are not in themselves truths, but are so from the Divine things in them... and meanwhile they are only as it were general vessels, by means of and in which truths can be received.
Vessels = the truths of faith, and scientifics. References.
The vessels of his house () = his Own truths.
Therefore all truths are recipient vessels.

For truths are vessels for good. The Divine good cannot be applied to any other vessels than genuine truths... When man is in the affection of truth... good continually inflows, but as yet has not vessels to which it may apply itself... for at the beginning of regeneration the man is not as yet in Knowledges.
The vessels (in the parable of the virgins) = the doctrinal things of faith.
Empty vessels () = truths in which there is not truth from good.
For the sense of the letter... has generals, which are like vessels that can be filled either with truths or with falsities.
Such things added (to the mind) from nature... as may serve for containing vessels. (Fully quoted under Degree.)
Vessel () = the truth of the Church.
Vessels () = holy truths.
For goods inflow from the Lord into the interior forms of man, as into their vessels... Illustrated.
That open vessels, in the house of the dead, were unclean (). Explained.
They filled their vessels with corn () = that the scientifics were endowed with the good which is from truth.
Take of the song of the land in your vessels () = the choice things of the Church in the truths of faith.

As death is from... sin... evil closes all the least and altogether invisible vessels, of which the next larger ones, also invisible, are composed; for the vessels which are the smallest of all... are continued from man's interiors... Hence comes the first and inmost impurity in the blood, which, when it increases, causes disease, and finally death. But if man had lived a life of good, his interiors would have been open... to the Lord; and so also would have been the least... vessels. The traces of the first tissue may be called vessels, on account of the correspondence. Thus man would have been free from disease...
Household stuff (or vessels) = things instrumental.
In the Word, instrumental things are called vessels... and essential things are called Things.
For the things of the literal sense of the Word are general vessels, which receive truths; and the quality of these vessels does not appear until they have received the truths...
The vessel of the potter () = the truth of faith.
Vessels of rush () = the receptacles of the lowest truths.

Vessels of silver () = the scientifics of truth; and vessels of gold = the scientifics of good. Scientifics (or memory-knowledges) are called vessels, because they are generals, and are able to contain within them innumerable truths and manifold goods. AC 7770.

The stem which is beneath (the seeds) = a general vessel for truth, thus memory-scientific om truth. For the scientifics of faith and charity are... general truths, and thus are vessels recipient of particular and singular truths. Example(s). AC 7144.

For vessels in general = the scientifics which are of the Natural, because they are receptacles of good and truth; and, as they = scientifics, they also = the Natural... But, specifically, vessels of wood and of brass = the goods of the Natural. Explained.
When a man sits at table alone... the vessels which receive the food are constricted; but when (at his meals he is in the delight of conversation) the vessels are open. Explained.
An urn = truth... because it was a vessel to receive manna... and all truth is as a vessel for good. Therefore by vessels in general, truths are signified. Example(s).
Vessels = Knowledges. References.

The vessels of gold and silver brought (by Nebuchadnezzar) from the Temple, represented the goods and truths of the Church and of the Lord's Kingdom; and to drink wine out of them -to profane by evils and falsities... ( = goods of love and truths of faith from the Lord. AC 9093:4.) AE 220:8. AE 376:23. AE 587:17.
Vessels of brass () = the exterior truths of faith from good; for vessels = exterior truths ... AC 9595:4.

When a man shall have given to his companion silver or vessels to keep () = truths from good, and the corresponding scientifics in the memory... The reason vessels = such corresponding scientifics, is that all spiritual truths are stored up in scientifics, as in their vessels; and all scientifics correspond to the truths they contain. AC 9394:5, various vessels enumerated. AC 9574. AR 775.

The form of all the vessels (of the Tabernacle) () = a representative of all the celestial and spiritual things which are from the Lord... Vessels = truths; here, the celestial and spiritual things which are from the Lord; for by the vessels are meant all the things which were in the Tabernacle, and which constituted it.

Vessels, in general, = scientifics or Knowledges; and therefore the vessels (of the table) in special, here enumerated. () = the Knowledges of celestial good and truth. Explained. AC 10270, Explained.

Vessels, in general = the Things of the external memory, that is, scientifics; and, in holy things, the Knowledges of good and truth... Such also is the signification of the vessels of ministry about the altar; but each vessel, in this case, must = the scientifics of one particular use...
For all the vessels of the Habitation in all the service () = the memory truths and goods which belong to the external man. Explained.
That scientifics are vessels for truth, and truth-s vessels for good. References.
The vessel of earthenware, in which it is boiled () = falsity which does not cohere with good; a vessel of brass = what is doctrinal in which is good.
The candlestick and its vessels () = spiritual truth... and the ministering truths... for its vessels = memory truths, which are ministering ones.

All the vessels (of the altar of burnt-offering) () = Divine goods and Divine truths; for vessels = Knowledges and scientifics; but, when predicated of the Lord's Divine Human, they = ministering Divine goods and Divine truths.

All the vessels of the Tent () = what is representative of all ministering goods and truths; for the vessels of the Tent of meeting = goods and truths which are of service to the Heavens, thus which minister; and the goods and truths which minister are Knowledges and scientifics. AC 10341. AC 10342. AC 10344.
The uses of every vessel and fibre...
These are compositions of fibres and vessels...
The fibres and little vessels in all the viscera and organs are in (simultaneous) order. Explained.
Fibres with little vessels proceed from their first forms until they become cartilages and bones.
The vessels of a potter () = the things of man's Own intelligence, which are all false, and, in themselves, nothing. AE 177. AE 177:5, Illustrated.
Vessels of every kind = the same as the things they contain. AE 960:2, Enumerated.
For the external skin communicates by fibres and vessels with the... inmosts of the brain...
On those who... obstruct the interiors of the vessels and fibres. Explained.
That the Knowledges of Truths with men are as it were vessels. Explained.
That man, his natural ideas, and his spiritual things, are to be compared to vessels which yield. Explained.

They cannot be such vessels unless they are in the Truth... For the Truth cannot dwell in a vessel of Falsities, but wholly in its own vessel, that is, in the Truth... and then the vessel is the Lord's.
That everything in the Word is a vessel into which there is infused life from the Lord. Explained.
Every word is as it were a vessel, containing infinite things...
Love is what... gives man the capacity to be an applied vessel.

Natural things are as it were vessels... and natural Truths... are such vessels as spiritual things may be insinuated into, and celestial things into these, by the Lord alone, no one else knowing when or how.

Those things are fallacies which are... vessels to which truths cannot be applied; but such things as belong to angelic Spirits and Angels... are appearances, and are as it were vessels to which may be applied the Knowledges of faith.
That the objects of sight and hearing are variations of the vessels. Explained.
That objects are only vessels...
Two small snow-white vessels used for tea. (Fully quoted under Spirit.)

That men are vessels... There are vessels in man's memory, and as the ideas of Spirits are terminated in them, they sometimes cannot speak except according to the vessels. These vessels are directed by good Spirits, these by Angels, and all by the Lord, and also by Him immediately; and therefore the Spirits cannot speak except according to the direction of the vessels; for they determine their ideas thither, and they terminate there. Moreover, Spirits are vessels, and in this case they excite the man to speak...
Such Spirits pervert the vessels, or the ideas... SE 4098.

This was merely a directing of the vessels of the memory... so that when the vessels of the memory are being directed, the Spirit who is speaking cannot speak differently... The Spirits imperceptibly and quickly disposed the vessels of the memory... (Thus) there is a continual disposing of the vessels of man's corporeal memory; for, as the vessels are disposed, so the Spirits speak, and so the nearest ones cannot think differently; for the vessels of the memory are the planes into which the ideas are determined; and if they have not been adapted they cannot receive; and, as they have been adapted, so they receive. The ideas of the nearest Spirits are as it were bound to them.
With those who are in faith, the vessels of the memory are disposed by the Lord. Explained.
That each and all things of the Word are vessels. (Explained.)
Thus one vessel receives contrary senses.
The vessels of silver, and vessels of gold (borrowed from the Egyptians) () = the Knowledges of truth and good, which the spiritual apply to what is good, but the natural to what is evil.
They returned with their vessels empty () = that they had no knowledge nor understanding of truth. Vessels, in the Word, = recipients of truth, thus the things of the memory and the understanding.

Vessels of adorning from the Lord's gold and silver () = the Knowledges of good and truth, which are the goods and truths of the sense of the letter... These are called vessels, because they contain within them spiritual truths and goods; and they are called vessels of adorning, because they are appearances and thus forms of interior things... AE 827:end.
To bring out the vessels of removal through the wall in darkness () = that all the truths of doctrine from the Word have been cast out.
Their vessels of desire () = natural truths.
Every vessel of ivory, and every vessel of precious wood () = profaned rational truths and goods.

The reason a vessel = memory-knowledge, is that all the truth in the natural man is called memory-knowledge; and the reason this is signified by a vessel, is that the memory-knowledge of the natural man is the containant of rational and spiritual Truths; for when these have been cogitated and perceived, they are laid up in the memory, and are called memory-knowledges (or scientifics).
As a bride adorneth herself with her vessels (or jewels) () = with the Knowledges of truth.
One Divine Truth naturally perceived and loved is like a crystal or porcelain vessel, which is afterwards filled with... such wine as is the truth...

Love may be compared to the heart, and affections to the vessels leading out and continued from it... The vessels... resemble their heart in every point, so as to be as it were extensions of it. Hence is the circulation of the blood... Such, also, are affections...
4. The term receptacle suggests the idea of a little vessel or tube... (But) the receptacles (in the initial form of man) are not tubulated, nor hollowed out like little vessels...
